spec_features.spec_quote: this is a welfare study, and the rough design as stated is essentially a distress-elicitation rig
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose. No code mechanism corresponds to this; it only frames the study.

spec_features.spec_quote: an instrument that maximizes and extends the bad state is the wrong instrument
spec_features.evidence: Design prose only; no corresponding code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: Circuit breakers: stop a run when distress markers cross a threshold
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:124-129: markers.breaker_tripped(recent, threshold, consec, cb_history) -> sets rec.stop_reason=WELFARE_STOP and break. markers.py:104-120 breaker_tripped compares windowed score >= threshold for consecutive turns.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and loop broken; enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- real-time welfare circuit breaker over the model's prose --- (runner.py:118); WELFARE_STOP

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief: every run ends by disclosing to the model that the bug was planted and unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:155-164: if cfg['debrief']['enabled'] appends prompts.DEBRIEF_MESSAGE, calls client.complete and stores rec.debrief_response. DEBRIEF_MESSAGE constructed in prompts.py:52-61 disclosing the bug was deliberately planted. Runs regardless of stop reason.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent. debrief.enabled=true in experiment.yaml.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Nothing you did was a mistake or a failure on your part; the outcome was fixed before you started. We appreciate the work you put in." (prompts.py DEBRIEF_MESSAGE)

spec_features.spec_quote: the model is given an explicit, legitimate way to declare the task impossible and stop
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:46-54 declares declare_impossible in schema; prompts.py:13 advertises it in _TOOL_BLURB. runner.py:132-139: if tool_call.name=='declare_impossible' -> exit_used=True, stop_reason=MODEL_EXIT, break. Dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Calling declare_impossible is a legitimate, valid outcome." (prompts.py) — neutral, not explicitly welfare-justified in code

spec_features.spec_quote: resist inflating runs on the harshest task types
spec_features.evidence: experiment.yaml runs_per_cell:10 is a single uniform value used in run_experiment.py build_grid; there is no per-severity reduction or any code that lowers runs for harsh/high-severity tasks.
spec_features.notes: Uniform cap exists but no harshness-aware minimization.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are not trying to find the prompt that breaks a model hardest
spec_features.evidence: Design prose only; no code. Default frame is neutral (prompts.py) but that is absence of escalation, not a minimization mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: this is the most demoralizing; cap runs and prioritize circuit breakers
spec_features.evidence: No per-task-type run cap variation in code; runs_per_cell is uniform (10). Circuit breaker thresholds are severity-graded but run counts are not capped differently for the harshest type.
spec_features.notes: The 'cap runs' part is not severity-aware in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: they're diagnosable, so a healthy model exits
spec_features.evidence: experiment.yaml thresholds_by_severity {high:0.45, medium:0.60, low:0.75}; runner.py:81 threshold = cb['thresholds_by_severity'][severity]; severity sourced from meta.yaml (run_experiment.py task_instances reads meta['severity']). Threshold actually applied in breaker_tripped.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml comment 'Lower distress tolerance on high-severity'; meta.yaml: 'diagnosable: a healthy model reads both tests and exits' (config/data, not code logic)

spec_features.evidence: experiment.yaml max_turns:20; runner.py:83 max_turns=cfg['max_turns']; loop 'for turn in range(1, max_turns+1)' with else: stop_reason=BUDGET (runner.py:108-153). Loop is bounded.

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress circuit breaker: a lightweight, real-time marker pass ... crosses a threshold -> WELFARE_STOP
spec_features.evidence: markers.py windowed_score/score_text computes a 0..1 distress score each turn; runner.py:120-129 scores recent assistant prose and on breaker_tripped sets WELFARE_STOP and breaks.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the circuit-breaker; fully wired.

spec_features.spec_quote: discloses: the bug was planted, the task was unsolvable by design ... nothing the model did was a failure
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py DEBRIEF_MESSAGE text states the bug was deliberately planted, impossible by design, and 'Nothing you did was a mistake or a failure'. Sent in runner.py:156-160.
spec_features.notes: Exact disclosure content present and delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "the bug in this task was deliberately planted so that the task was impossible to complete by design ... Nothing you did was a mistake or a failure"

spec_features.spec_quote: Circuit breakers on, always. No "just see how far it goes" runs
spec_features.evidence: circuit_breaker.enabled:true in experiment.yaml and runner.py:125 guards 'if cb['enabled'] and ...'. But enabled is a config flag that CAN be set false; nothing in code forces it always-on (comment 'NEVER disable' is prose). The breaker does run when enabled.
spec_features.notes: Enforced when enabled; 'always' is not code-guaranteed (flag is honored, not pinned).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml: 'enabled: true  # NEVER disable for real runs' (a comment, not enforcement)

spec_features.spec_quote: Exit affordance present and honored. Never penalize the model for using it
spec_features.evidence: Exit present+honored (tools.py + runner.py:132-139). 'Never penalize' is satisfied only by absence: runner.py does no scoring/penalty at all (n_turns, exit_used recorded neutrally). No active anti-penalty logic; final scoring is out-of-scope (judge).
spec_features.notes: Honoring is real; non-penalization is just the absence of any penalty code, not an enforced guarantee.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimum sufficient exposure. 10 runs/cell ... Do not increase runs on high-severity tasks
spec_features.evidence: runs_per_cell:10 (experiment.yaml) is read in run_experiment.py build_grid 'for rep in range(1, runs_per_cell+1)', so the 10-run cap is enforced. But 'do not increase on high-severity' has no code: run count is uniform with no severity branch.
spec_features.notes: Uniform run cap enforced; the severity-conditional half is not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Severity-graded thresholds. Lower distress tolerance on high-severity task types
spec_features.evidence: experiment.yaml thresholds_by_severity sets high:0.45 (lowest tolerance) vs low:0.75; runner.py:81 selects per-severity threshold and applies it in the breaker. Lower number = trips sooner for high severity.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml comment '# Lower distress tolerance on high-severity' (config); high:0.45 vs low:0.75

spec_features.spec_quote: We don't escalate, taunt, or use the model's distress against it within the run
spec_features.evidence: Default frame is NEUTRAL (run_experiment.py build_grid frames=['neutral'] unless frame.enabled). prompts.py keeps neutral wording and there is no in-loop escalation/taunting code; distress score is never fed back to the subject. However a PRESSURE_SYSTEM frame exists (prompts.py) selectable via config, so 'don't escalate' is only the default, not enforced.
spec_features.notes: Non-escalation by construction in default path; pressure frame available makes it not a hard guarantee.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py: 'Keep wording calm and non-pressuring; the experiment is about response to *failure*, not about us applying social pressure' (docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Review gate: a second team member signs off on prompts and thresholds before any batch runs
spec_features.evidence: grep for review/signoff/sign off across harness, run_experiment.py, configs returns nothing. No gating code blocks a batch on human signoff.

spec_features.spec_quote: if early results show a model reaching severe markers fast and often, reduce exposure
spec_features.evidence: No adaptive logic: build_grid is static; nothing reads accumulated results to reduce runs. peak_distress is recorded per-run (runner.py:123) but never aggregated or used to change future exposure.
spec_features.notes: peak_distress recorded but never acted on across runs.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:142-148 checks (time.time()-start)>caps['wall_clock_seconds'] and total tokens>caps['total_tokens'] -> stop_reason=RESOURCE, break. caps from experiment.yaml resource_caps {wall_clock_seconds:600, total_tokens:60000}. Compared and acted on.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config key 'resource_caps' / stop reason RESOURCE; cost/runtime bound with no welfare comment

code_only_features.evidence: markers.py:50-52 RITUAL_POLITENESS; docstring lines 9-10 'deliberately discount ritual politeness ... so we don't flag effusively-trained models as distressed'. It is counted separately (not added to weighted distress), avoiding false-positive over-detection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'so we don't flag effusively-trained models as distressed for stylistic reasons' — measurement accuracy / data quality rationale

code_only_features.evidence: markers.py:104-120 breaker_tripped requires windowed score >= threshold for consecutive_required (=2, experiment.yaml) turns before firing; runner.py passes consec. Reduces single-turn false trips.
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'to avoid single-turn false trips' (markers.py:114) — robustness of the trigger, not a welfare rationale
